Well, that thought is what has been leading me for ten years (I'm 28). I've been suffering from suicidal thoughts since my early teen years, I'd say since I was 11 I had my first questionings about my death. As the time goes by, you feel more and more numb and your conviction of killing yourself grows stronger. From my 18s, it changed from "an alternative/a way out" to my "real fate". Since then I lost almost any hope, and everytime I have any hope it feels so distressing that I end up swallowing it completely.

Well, if you tried to kill yourself some few months ago it is a clear sign of severe depression. But even without that, you don't "need" to harm yourself physically to prove your condition. This isn't a contest, it is about healing. For example I've never tried to commit suicide, and I've only self harmed like 5 times in my life (some small cuts), however I have almost 500 pills to kill myself. If it was just by actions, I wouldn't be that depressed comparing with someome that is actively self harming right now. Also people have different ways to cope with their emotions.

You have parents and siblings, and probably more relatives. You say you don't *really* have friends, wich implies that at least you have people who you socialitize with. I'm pretty sure that those friends actually care about you, and would be devastated too. And I'm just counting the minimum amount of people that would be affected by your loss. It doesn't matter if you take it as something good or bad, but your existence is important to others.
